Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: embedding migration scope

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on tech/ops items before we draft the MAP: 

Call highlights:
- ClearBay will migrate search/recommendation embeddings off current vendor to Redwood for 3 production services (search, related items, personalization scoring).
- Primary constraints: vector dim target, batching latency envelope (p95 sub-60ms for retrieval traffic), and auth integration with ClearBay's internal proxy.

Immediate asks from the call (owner / target):
1) Confirm current vector profile: sample file attached (cb_vector_sample.csv). If the sample is representative, looks like 384 dims but there were cases at 256/512. Can you confirm canonical dimension? (Anna / Tue 11/30)
2) Auth flow: ClearBay uses an internal OAuth proxy + mTLS to talk to external vendors. We recommended token-based routing with a short-lived Redwood client token + IP allowlist. We'll follow up with a tech sketch. (Redwood / Wed 12/01)
3) Batching and normalization: we recommended per-request batching up to 64 vectors with L2-normalize-on-ingest option; Priyom to validate throughput numbers vs ClearBay's QPS. (Priyom / Wed 12/01)

Attachments: cb_vector_sample.csv (sample vectors), preliminary embed profile (redwood_embed_profile_v1.json), draft MAP (ClearBay-MAP-v1.docx).

Proposed next call: 30 min technical handoff (engineers only) — Wed 12/01 11:00 PT. Is that OK?

Hi Anna — quick technical notes ahead of today's handoff. I attached a compact embed profile and a small throughput matrix; pasted key points below.

1) Dimension handling
- Redwood supports on-the-fly projection for 384->512 or 512->384 using a learned linear transform during migration to minimize re-index costs. That said, for best recall we recommend canonicalizing to 512 and re-embedding historical items in batches (we can do incremental re-indexing to avoid a full downtime).

2) Batching & latency
- For retrieval traffic with p95 <= 60ms we recommend: max batch size=32 for synchronous retrieval (lower per-request latency), or async batch=64 for bulk reindexing jobs. Continuous batching with per-customer windows will improve throughput while keeping tail latency bounded.

3) Normalization + reranker
- Normalize vectors to unit length on ingest (L2), store un-normalized copies if you plan to run custom dot-product rerankers. Redwood supports both normalized and raw vectors as separate fields to enable both similarity measures.

4) Auth & routing
- We can support proxy-backed OAuth by issuing a short-lived Redwood service token after a proxy validation webhook. mTLS client cert checks can be enforced at the VPC/private connector level for Private deployments; for Hosted we recommend a token+IP allowlist pattern.

Attachments included: redwood_embed_profile_v1.json (profile), cb_throughput_estimates.xlsx (throughput matrix) — I've uploaded the profile to the shared Drive link in the thread.

See you at 11:00 PT. I'll cover SDK snippets for batching + normalization and a minimal migration playbook.

- Priyom
